page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an ARM64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor family. It features 2 shared vCPUs consisting of 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, equating to 1.95 GB per core, and includes 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No dedicated GPU resources or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-level performance characteristics. The stress-ng single-core CPU test shows average performance in the middle 50% tier at 1821.28, but multi-core performance drops to the bottom 25% tier with a score of 3610.67. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 131.92 GB/sec in the bottom 10% tier and large block uncached read bandwidth at 25.88 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect these limitations, yielding a single-core score of 1014.0 and a multi-core score of 1826.0, both falling into the lower performance tiers.

The cax11 server offers a highly cost-efficient entry point into ARM64 cloud computing, utilizing shared CPU resources to minimize overhead. However, the shared CPU allocation and lower memory bandwidth present clear performance tradeoffs, particularly for memory-intensive or highly parallel workloads. Cryptographic execution is supported via hardware AES, but extended instruction sets and vector operations are limited, as shown by a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 1465.18.

Given its resource profile, the Hetzner Cloud cax11 is recommended for lightweight, non-critical applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, simple text processing, and low-traffic database operations. It is not recommended for memory-heavy databases, large-scale compilation, or complex mathematical modeling.
